pitchCoding.rule: every bar has a local key (tonic, mode); index = pitch - tonic_ref(tonic) + 65 with tonic_ref in MIDI 54..65; pitch = index - 65 + tonic_ref (exact inverse)
pitchCoding.classes: 139 relative indices (any MIDI pitch in any key) + unpitched; inputs add scale degree x mode, sounding octave and the key
pitchCoding.output: full relative-pitch head + scale-degree head + sounding-octave head + priors (interval from the voice per group, sounding/bass/chord pitch classes, chord-relative, mode scale); classes outside MIDI 0..127 are excluded in training and generation
pitchCoding.evidence: 17,001 target pitches of 44 real windows (five sources, random transposition) decode to the source pitch: 0 mismatches; same melody in C and D has the same codes (test)

tonalLabels.keys: KeyTracker for every source: bar pitch-class histograms (lowest note of each onset x1.5), Lieder-derived key profiles, key-signature bonus for scores, Viterbi with fifths-distance change cost
tonalLabels.chords: AugmentedNet for aligned Lieder (937 of 1,131); ChordTracker elsewhere: beat segments, 9 qualities covering 99.8% of Lieder labels, bass/diatonic priors, Viterbi
tonalLabels.note: labels are estimates, not ground truth; the tracker key regions are steadier than AugmentedNet tonicizations, which matches key-walking in the console

architecture.events: one backbone step per note, chord change or bar end; chord changes precede the notes at their onset; within an onset unpitched notes, then pitched notes from the lowest up (bass before melody)
architecture.decoder: kind -> onset position in the bar (REMI-style; logits masked to the legal range in training as in generation) -> chord root (relative) -> quality | group -> voice pointer -> pitch -> duration -> expression; chord heads on chord rows and note heads on note rows only; inputs include a note's interval above the chord root and the interval by which its voice reached its previous note
architecture.attention: rotary in event index, musical time (quarters), beat phase and bar phase; 12 of 16 pairs rotated, 4 content-only; ring-buffer cache of 512 events
architecture.planner: causal pre-norm transformer over up to 511 completed bars with rotary positions over bar distance (periods 2..256 bars on 8 of 16 pairs); streamed with a cache at generation (one step per bar). Per bar: scale degrees in its key, group shares, density, mean pitch, mode, tonic step, 16-bin onset rhythm, top-voice and bass scale-degree histograms, phrase phases over 4 and 16 bars (78 values)
architecture.barControls: meter, tempo, key, modulation step, corpus style, requested groups, requested density (learned; groups/density dropped 50%, style 30% in training)
architecture.barObjectives: next key relative to the current tonic (from the plan), scale degrees, density, register and groups of the bar (plan + modulation)
architecture.initialization: random (GPT-style normal 0.02; residual outputs, copy biases and priors start at zero); the v2 partial transfer was removed: in short runs on the same windows it trailed random initialization in total loss (lr 3e-4, steps 191-240: 14.01 vs 12.88; lr 1e-3, steps 115-164 where the v2 run stopped: 13.44 vs 12.62), better on pitch early but worse on onsets and durations
architecture.learningRate: 1e-3 default (best of 3e-4 and 1e-3 from scratch in 240-step runs), 300 warmup steps, cosine to 0.1x

referenceBars.selection: most similar earlier bar within the planner history: Jaccard of key-relative (onset on a 1/24-quarter grid, relative pitch) items >= 0.5, ties to the most recent; otherwise none
referenceBars.corpusStatistics: whole pieces (40 Lieder, 40 classical scores, 30 MIDI): about 40% of score bars have Jaccard >= 0.5 with an earlier bar, 22% >= 0.9; most common distances 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 bars, and in classical scores 37% of such references lie 99 or more bars back
referenceBars.pointer: column 0 = none, column 1 + h = earlier bar h: scaled dot product of the new bar's plan and earlier planner states plus a learned bias per distance bucket (1, 2, 3, 4, 5-7, 8, 9-15, 16, 17-31, 32, 33-63, 64, 65+); objective bar_ref, weight 0.25
referenceBars.decoderInputs: before kind/onset: the reference's next onset and how many of its notes remain at the current onset; after the onset: group, relative pitch and duration of the reference note with the same rank among the notes at that onset, and the scale degrees the reference sounds there; each also a learned copy bias on the onset, group, pitch (per group) and duration logits
referenceBars.dropout: the decoder loses its reference in 20% of training bars; the pointer target is kept
referenceBars.generation: reference='auto' samples the pointer over the last 511 bars, an integer names a bar, None disables it
referenceBars.windowShare: full score sweep: 20,783 of 58,592 window bars (35.5%) have a reference
referenceBars.alignedAgreement: 44 real windows: for notes in bars with a reference, the aligned reference gives the actual onset 82-93%, pitch 40-84%, duration 69-90% of the time depending on the source

fourPillars.harmony: explicit chord events with key-relative roots and 40 qualities; current chord in every note input and decoder state; chord-relative and chord-tone pitch priors; sounding scale degrees and bass degree; mode scale prior; key and modulation controls and objective
fourPillars.polyphony: voice pointer over 64 slots with recency/sounding features; pitch conditioned on the voice, its previous note, the interval that reached it and a group-specific interval prior; onset ordered bass upward; a part that changes instrument group opens a new voice, as in generation
fourPillars.form: reference bars (pointer + aligned copy inputs) let a bar restate any of the last 511 bars, far beyond the event window; causal rotary planner over 511 key-relative bar summaries with rhythm, outer-voice and phrase features; every window event trained with its own bar plan; musical-time and bar-phase attention; no section labels exist
fourPillars.orchestration: six native groups chosen before voice and pitch, learned group/density requests plus hard masks, sounding-octave pitch head for instrument ranges, next-bar group objective, explicit MIDI drum keys, source-known expression masks; corpus-style condition (classical/contemporary symphony, curated MIDI, Lieder, classical scores), like the joint model style input

rule.note: scores: notated values with a preferred denominator stay exact, others snap to the simplest preferred fraction within tolerance. MIDI: chord spreading within the chord window joins the first onset and near-grid durations snap to simple values first. Vocabulary = most frequent resulting values (zero always included).
